First, load in the water supply database. 
We are only performing this rapid assessment on CONUS water supplies that are not municipal or hauled water supplies.
```{r}
# parks <- getParkSystem()
# read in pre-saved park file
suppressMessages(parks <- st_read("data/rapid/inputs/park_boundaries_2025-08-14.gpkg"))

park_water_supplies <- parks %>% 
  st_centroid() %>% 
  st_transform(4326) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(y = st_coordinates(.)[,2], x = st_coordinates(.)[,1])

# Read in water supply database for filtered parks


table_path <- "data/Water_Supply_Systems/NPS_Water_Systems_Database_Joined.xlsx"


water_supplies <- read_excel(table_path,
                             sheet = 1,
                             na = c("NA", "U"),
                             skip = 1) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    source_longitude = as.numeric(source_longitude),
    source_latitude = as.numeric(source_latitude)
  ) %>%
  filter(!state %in% c("AK", "AS", "HI", "MP", "PR", "VI")) %>%
  left_join(
    park_water_supplies %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::select(UNIT_CODE, x, y),
    by = c(park_unit = "UNIT_CODE")
  ) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    coords_flag = ifelse(
      is.na(source_longitude) |
        is.na(source_latitude),
      "Centroid",
      "Source Coordinates"
    ),
    source_longitude = ifelse(is.na(source_longitude), x, source_longitude),
    source_latitude = ifelse(is.na(source_latitude), y, source_latitude)
  ) %>%
  # remove municipal and hauled source types, accounting for database entry errors
  filter(!str_detect(source_type, regex("municipal|hauled", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>%
  drop_na(source_longitude, source_latitude) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = (c("source_longitude", "source_latitude")),
           crs = 4326,
           remove = FALSE)
```

# Parkwide Exploration

Grab visitation across the entire National Park Service so what the trends are like nationally:

```{r}
system_visitation <- getParkwideVisitation(startYear = 2010, endYear = 2024) 
# for single park instead, use this - 
# system_visitation <- getUnitVisitation(unit = "MISS", startYear = 2010, endYear = 2024) 

# seasonal breakdown
system_visitation <- system_visitation %>%
  mutate(date = ym(paste0(Year, "-", Month)),
         season = case_when(Month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
                            Month %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Spring",
                            Month %in% c(6, 7, 8) ~ "Summer",
                            Month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall"),
         month_name = month.abb[Month],
         season_month = factor(paste0(season, "_", month_name),
                               levels = c("Winter_Jan","Winter_Feb","Spring_Mar","Spring_Apr","Spring_May",
                                          "Summer_Jun","Summer_Jul","Summer_Aug",
                                          "Fall_Sep","Fall_Oct","Fall_Nov",
                                          "Winter_Dec")))

# annual stats
system_annual_visitation <- system_visitation %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarize(total_visitation = sum(RecreationVisitors))

ggplot(system_visitation, aes(x = factor(Year), y = RecreationVisitors)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(color = ifelse(Year %in% c(2020, 2021), "COVID", "NonCOVID")),  
               outlier.shape = NA,
               fill = NA,  
               size = 1) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = season_month),
              width = 0.2,
              alpha = 0.7,
              size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("NonCOVID" = "grey70",
                                "COVID"    = "tan",
                                "Winter_Jan" = "#9ecae1", "Winter_Feb" = "#3182bd",
                                "Spring_Mar" = "#006d2c", "Spring_Apr" = "#31a354", "Spring_May" = "#a1d99b",
                                "Summer_Jun" = "#fbb4b9", "Summer_Jul" = "#f768a1", "Summer_Aug" = "#ae017e",
                                "Fall_Sep"   = "#fee08b", "Fall_Oct"  = "#fdae61", "Fall_Nov"  = "#d73027",
                                "Winter_Dec" = "#deebf7"),
                     breaks = c("Winter_Jan","Winter_Feb","Spring_Mar","Spring_Apr","Spring_May",
                                "Summer_Jun","Summer_Jul","Summer_Aug",
                                "Fall_Sep","Fall_Oct","Fall_Nov","Winter_Dec"),
                     labels = c("Winter_Jan" = "January",  "Winter_Feb" = "February",
                                "Spring_Mar" = "March",    "Spring_Apr" = "April",   "Spring_May" = "May",
                                "Summer_Jun" = "June",     "Summer_Jul" = "July",    "Summer_Aug" = "August",
                                "Fall_Sep"   = "September","Fall_Oct"  = "October", "Fall_Nov"   = "November",
                                "Winter_Dec" = "December")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Recreation Visitors", color = "Month") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1))
```

### Explore Total Park Visitation Through Time

*Fit a simple linear regression of total annual visitation on year*

```{r}
linear_model <- lm((total_visitation) ~ Year, data = system_annual_visitation)

summary(linear_model)

# plot(linear_model)

# intercept
intercept <- coef(linear_model)[1]
# visits/year
slope <- coef(linear_model)[2]
r_squared <- summary(linear_model)$r.squared
adj_r_squared <- summary(linear_model)$adj.r.squared

avg_visitation <- mean(system_annual_visitation$total_visitation)

# average annual growth rate (scaled to mean visitation)
annual_growth_rate <- (slope / avg_visitation) * 100

# predictions for historical data
system_annual_visitation$predicted <- predict(linear_model)
system_annual_visitation$residuals <- residuals(linear_model)

predictions <- predict(linear_model, newdata = tibble(Year =  2024:2100), interval = "prediction", level = 0.95)

future_predictions <- tibble(Year = 2024:2100,
                             predicted_visitation = predictions[,1],
                             lower_95 = predictions[,2],
                             upper_95 = predictions[,3])

milestones <- future_predictions %>% filter(Year %in% c(2024, 2035, 2050, 2065, 2100))

# tremd through time
ggplot(system_annual_visitation, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = total_visitation/1000000), color = "blue", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = predicted/1000000), color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = future_predictions, aes(x = Year, y = predicted_visitation/1000000), 
             color = "red", size = 2, shape = 17) +
  geom_ribbon(data = future_predictions, aes(x = Year, ymin = lower_95/1000000, ymax = upper_95/1000000), 
              alpha = 0.2, fill = "red") +
  labs(title = "NPS Parkwide Visitation",
       subtitle = paste("R² =", round(r_squared, 3), "  Annual Growth Rate =", round(annual_growth_rate, 2), "%"),
       x = "Year", 
       y = "Annual Visits (Millions)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2100, 10))
```

### Explore Seasonality of Visitation Through Time

*Explore how the percentage distribution of visitors by month changes (or hasn't) through time, COVID years removed...*

Parkwide totals indicate that visitors are showing up across more months through time. As in, visitation window is widening...

```{r, echo = TRUE}
# monthly percentages for each year (excluding COVID years 2020-2021)
monthly_percentages <- system_visitation %>%
  filter(!Year %in% c(2020, 2021)) %>%  # Remove COVID years
  group_by(Year) %>%
  mutate(annual_total = sum(RecreationVisitors),
         monthly_percentage = (RecreationVisitors / annual_total) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

# statistics by month across all years
monthly_summary <- monthly_percentages %>%
  group_by(month_name, Month) %>%
  summarize(mean_pct = mean(monthly_percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_pct = median(monthly_percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_pct = sd(monthly_percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_pct = min(monthly_percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_pct = max(monthly_percentage, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Month)

# monthly percentages over time
ggplot(monthly_percentages, aes(x = Year, y = factor(Month, levels = 12:1, 
                                                     labels = rev(month.abb)), 
                                fill = monthly_percentage)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "% of Annual\nVisits") +
  labs(title = "Monthly Visitation Distribution Over Time",
       subtitle = "Percentage of annual visits occurring in each month",
       x = "Year", 
       y = "Month") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# coefficient of variation over time to see if seasonality is becoming more/less pronounced
seasonal_variation <- monthly_percentages %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarize(cv_monthly = sd(monthly_percentage) / mean(monthly_percentage) * 100,
            range_pct = max(monthly_percentage) - min(monthly_percentage),
            .groups = 'drop')

ggplot(seasonal_variation, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cv_monthly), color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = cv_monthly), method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Seasonality Strength Over Time",
       subtitle = "Coefficient of variation in monthly percentages",
       x = "Year", 
       y = "Coefficient of Variation (%)") +
  theme_minimal()

decade_comparison <- monthly_percentages %>%
  mutate(decade = floor(Year / 5) * 5) %>%
  filter(decade %in% c(1980, 1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020)) %>%
  group_by(decade, month_name, Month) %>%
  summarise(mean_pct = mean(monthly_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

ggplot(decade_comparison, aes(x = reorder(month_name, Month), y = mean_pct, 
                              color = factor(decade))) +
  geom_line(aes(group = decade), size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Distribution by Time Period",
       subtitle = "Average percentage of annual visits by month and time period",
       x = "Month", 
       y = "% of Annual Visits",
       color = "Time Period") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# test for overall change in seasonality
seasonality_trend <- lm(cv_monthly ~ Year, data = seasonal_variation)
cat(sprintf("\nOverall seasonality trend: %s (p = %.3f)\n", 
            ifelse(coef(seasonality_trend)[2] > 0, "Increasing", "Decreasing"),
            summary(seasonality_trend)$coefficients[2,4]))
```

### Miscellaneous

*What's the largest visitation year for parks?*

```{r, echo = FALSE}
units <- parks %>%
  pull(UNIT_CODE)

peak_year_finder <- function(park_unit){
  park_visitation <- getUnitVisitation(units = park_unit, startYear = 1970, endYear = 2024) %>%
    group_by(UnitCode, Year) %>%
    summarize(RecreationVisitors = sum(RecreationVisitors), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(RecreationVisitors == max(RecreationVisitors, na.rm = TRUE)) 
}

highest_year <- units %>%
  map(possibly(~ peak_year_finder(.), otherwise = NULL)) %>%
  keep(~!is.null(.)) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  left_join(., parks, by = c("UnitCode" = "UNIT_CODE")) %>%
  mutate(`Park Type` = ifelse(UNIT_TYPE == "National Park", "National Park", "Other Designation"))

ggplot(data = highest_year) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(x = Year, fill = `Park Type`), breaks = 1970:2024) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Park-specific "simple" visitation exposure

Visitation-based exposure by fitting linear trends to annual NPS visitation (2010–2024) for each park, using predicted 2024 visitation as a baseline and projecting visitation to 2050. Parks with positive, "unconstrained" trends use their observed historical growth, while parks with timed entry, negative trends, or trends less than a "baseline" growth instead apply this baseline growth rate of 0.87% per year (NPS average) or I've also landed on something more conservative like 0.25% (this can be changed). Exposure is represented by the percent change in visitation from 2024 to 2050. A second indicator captures seasonality changes (ie widening of visitation window) by calculating the year-to-year coefficient of variation (CV) of monthly visitation shares (excluding COVID years), modeling how this CV changes over time, and projecting it to 2050. As it is, the indicator created for seasonality is only highlighting parks where the visitation window is widening, tho a narrowing visitation window would also be something interesting to capture. (APPA, CAJO, CEBE, EBLA truly have no visitation data - so these are NA in the final data frame.)
```{r}
park_visitation <- calc_visitation_exposure(water_supplies = water_supplies %>% select(park_name, park_unit),
                                            baseline_growth_rate = 0.0025,
                                            baseline_seasonality_shift = 1, # 1 = no mod to the park's raw CV trend
                                            save = FALSE,
                                            output_dir = NULL,
                                            verbose = TRUE)
```

```{r}
ggplot(park_visitation %>% distinct(park_unit, slope_adjustment), aes(x = slope_adjustment, fill = slope_adjustment)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Trend treatment",
       y = "Number of parks",
       title = "Parks and their trends") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

#### SLM exploration

Fancy AI fig to compare un-capped vs capped growth at timed-entry parks. 

```{r}
# Enhanced comparison visualization function for all baseline scenarios
compare_trend_methods <- function(park_unit, 
                                  timed_entry_year = NULL,
                                  baseline_growth_rate = 0.0025,
                                  insufficient_data_threshold = 14 * 12) {
  
  # grab visitation data
  visitation <- getUnitVisitation(units = park_unit, startYear = 2010, endYear = 2024)
  
  annual_visitation <- visitation %>%
    group_by(Year) %>%
    summarize(total = sum(RecreationVisitors), .groups = "drop")
  
  # OG method (full trend 2010-2024 extrapolated to 2050)
  lm_original <- lm(total ~ Year, data = annual_visitation)
  original_slope <- coef(lm_original)[2]
  intercept <- coef(lm_original)[1]
  
  pred_2024 <- annual_visitation %>% filter(Year == 2024) %>% pull(total)
  pred_2050_orig <- predict(lm_original, newdata = data.frame(Year = 2050))
  pct_change_orig <- (pred_2050_orig - pred_2024) / pred_2024
  
  # Check all conditions for baseline adjustment
  negative_trend <- original_slope < 0
  has_timed_entry <- !is.null(timed_entry_year)
  insufficient_data <- nrow(visitation) < insufficient_data_threshold
  
  baseline_slope <- pred_2024 * baseline_growth_rate
  below_baseline <- original_slope < baseline_slope
  
  use_baseline <- negative_trend || has_timed_entry || insufficient_data || below_baseline
  
  # Determine reason for adjustment (priority order)
  reason <- case_when(
    insufficient_data ~ "insufficient_data",
    negative_trend ~ "negative_trend",
    has_timed_entry ~ "timed_entry",
    below_baseline ~ "below_baseline",
    TRUE ~ "none"
  )
  
  # Create label for baseline method
  baseline_label <- paste0("Baseline Growth (", baseline_growth_rate*100, "% annually)")
  
  # Create original prediction line (2010-2050)
  pred_data_orig <- data.frame(Year = 2010:2050) %>%
    mutate(predicted = predict(lm_original, newdata = .),
           method = "Original (Unadjusted)")
  
  # Adjusted method with baseline growth
  pred_data_adjusted <- NULL
  
  if(use_baseline) {
    projection_slope <- baseline_slope
    
    pred_data_adjusted <- data.frame(Year = 2010:2050) %>%
      mutate(predicted = case_when(
        Year <= 2024 ~ predict(lm_original, newdata = data.frame(Year = Year)),
        Year > 2024 ~ pred_2024 + (projection_slope * (Year - 2024))
      ),
      method = baseline_label)
    
    pred_2050_adj <- pred_2024 + (projection_slope * (2050 - 2024))
    pct_change_adj <- (pred_2050_adj - pred_2024) / pred_2024
    
    subtitle_text <- sprintf(
      "Original: %.1f%% | Baseline Growth (+%.1f%% annually): +%.1f%% | Change (2024-2050)",
      pct_change_orig * 100, baseline_growth_rate*100, pct_change_adj * 100
    )
  } else {
    subtitle_text <- sprintf("Projected change 2024-2050: %.1f%%", pct_change_orig * 100)
  }
  
  # Combine prediction data
  pred_data <- if(!is.null(pred_data_adjusted)) {
    bind_rows(pred_data_orig, pred_data_adjusted)
  } else {
    pred_data_orig
  }
  
  # Create named vectors for scales
  color_values <- c("Original (Unadjusted)" = "#2166ac")
  color_values[baseline_label] <- "#1b7837"
  
  linetype_values <- c("Original (Unadjusted)" = "dashed")
  linetype_values[baseline_label] <- "solid"
  
  # Create plot
  p1 <- ggplot() +
    # Historical data points
    geom_point(data = annual_visitation, aes(x = Year, y = total), 
               size = 3, alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
    # Trend lines
    geom_line(data = pred_data, aes(x = Year, y = predicted, color = method, linetype = method),
              linewidth = 1.2) +
    # Future projection zone
    annotate("rect", xmin = 2024, xmax = 2050, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "gray90", alpha = 0.3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = color_values) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = linetype_values)
  
  # Build caption based on reason for adjustment
  caption_text <- case_when(
    reason == "insufficient_data" ~ paste0(
      "Note: Insufficient historical data (", nrow(visitation), " months, < ", 
      insufficient_data_threshold, " required). Baseline growth (", 
      baseline_growth_rate*100, "%) applied based on NPS system-wide trends."
    ),
    reason == "negative_trend" ~ paste0(
      "Note: Negative historical trend replaced with ", baseline_growth_rate*100, 
      "% baseline growth based on long-term NPS system-wide trends."
    ),
    reason == "timed_entry" ~ paste0(
      "Note: Timed entry management constrains future growth; baseline rate (", 
      baseline_growth_rate*100, "%) applied based on system-wide trends."
    ),
    reason == "below_baseline" ~ paste0(
      "Note: Historical growth rate below NPS system baseline. Baseline rate (", 
      baseline_growth_rate*100, "%) applied for conservative future projection."
    ),
    TRUE ~ ""  # Changed from NULL to empty string
  )
  
  p1 <- p1 +
    labs(title = paste("Visitation Trends:", park_unit),
         subtitle = subtitle_text,
         x = "Year", 
         y = "Annual Recreation Visitors",
         color = "Projection Method",
         linetype = "Projection Method",
         caption = if(caption_text != "") caption_text else NULL) +  # Only add caption if not empty
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray40"),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0, color = "gray50", 
                                      margin = margin(t = 10)),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2050, by = 5))
  
  # Add vertical line for timed entry year if provided
  if(has_timed_entry && reason == "timed_entry") {
    p1 <- p1 + 
      geom_vline(xintercept = timed_entry_year, linetype = "dotted", 
                 color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 1) +
      annotate("text", x = timed_entry_year, y = max(annual_visitation$total) * 1.05,
               label = paste("Timed Entry\n", timed_entry_year),
               hjust = 0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", color = "darkgreen")
  }
  
  # Add 2024 marker
  p1 <- p1 +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2024, linetype = "solid", 
               color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
    annotate("text", x = 2024, y = min(annual_visitation$total) * 0.95,
             label = "2024\n(Present)", hjust = 0.5, size = 3, color = "gray30")
  
  # Add trend indicator annotation with color coding
  trend_color <- case_when(
    reason == "negative_trend" ~ "darkred",
    reason == "timed_entry" ~ "darkgreen",
    reason == "insufficient_data" ~ "darkorange",
    reason == "below_baseline" ~ "darkgoldenrod",
    TRUE ~ "gray40"
  )
  
  trend_tag <- case_when(
    reason == "negative_trend" ~ " (NEGATIVE)",
    reason == "timed_entry" ~ " (CONSTRAINED)",
    reason == "insufficient_data" ~ " (LIMITED DATA)",
    reason == "below_baseline" ~ " (BELOW BASELINE)",
    TRUE ~ ""
  )
  
  trend_label <- paste0(
    "Historical Trend: ", 
    ifelse(original_slope >= 0, "+", ""),
    scales::comma(round(original_slope, 0)), 
    " visitors/year",
    trend_tag
  )
  
  p1 <- p1 +
    annotate("text", x = 2010, y = max(annual_visitation$total) * 0.88,
             label = trend_label, hjust = 0, size = 3.5, 
             fontface = "bold.italic",
             color = trend_color)
  
  return(p1)
}

# Example usage for each scenario:

# 1. Timed entry park
compare_trend_methods(park_unit = "ROMO", timed_entry_year = 2020)

# 2. Negative trend park
compare_trend_methods(park_unit = "YOSE")  # Replace with actual park code

# 3. Below baseline growth park
compare_trend_methods(park_unit = "OLYM")  # Replace with actual park code

# 4. Insufficient data park
compare_trend_methods(park_unit = "FRST")  # Replace with actual park code
```

#### Exposure scores

Park visitation trends

```{r, echo = FALSE}
sample_park_visitation <- park_visitation %>% 
  filter(park_unit != "HATU")

mapview(sample_park_visitation,
  zcol = "visit_raw_pct_change",
  layer.name = "Percent Increase in Visitation: 2024-2050",
  col.regions = colorRampPalette(c("yellow", "orange", "red")))
# decreasing percent means visitor window is shrinking
mapview(sample_park_visitation,
        zcol = "visit_raw_cv_change",
        layer.name = "Percent Change in Visitor Window: 2024-2050",
        col.regions = colorRampPalette(c("black", "red", "orange", "yellow"))(50))

# Create a diverging color palette function
diverging_palette <- function(x) {
  # Split into negative and positive
  breaks <- seq(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 101)
  zero_idx <- which.min(abs(breaks))
  
  # Colors for negative values (blue to black)
  neg_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "black"))(zero_idx)
  # Colors for positive values (black to red, orange, yellow)
  pos_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("black", "red", "orange", "yellow"))(101 - zero_idx)
  
  return(c(neg_colors, pos_colors))
}
```

CV trends 
the more negative (bluer), the tighter the visitation window gets. The more positive (yellower), the wider the visitation window gets. 

Blue to black (negative), then black to red to orange to yellow (positive)

```{r}
mapview(park_visitation,
        zcol = "visit_raw_cv_change",
        layer.name = "Percent Change in Visitor Window: 2024-2050",
        at = seq(min(park_visitation$visit_raw_cv_change, na.rm = TRUE),
                 max(park_visitation$visit_raw_cv_change, na.rm = TRUE),
                 length.out = 101),
        col.regions = diverging_palette(park_visitation$visit_raw_cv_change),
        legend = FALSE)

```

#### Change in seasonality examples

Example of widening (top figure) and narrowing (bottom figure) park visitation season:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Identify top 5 and bottom 5 parks by change in CV
top_bottom_cv <- park_visitation %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  arrange(desc(visit_raw_cv_change)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(obs_2024)) %>%
  mutate(rank_group = case_when(
    row_number() <= 10 ~ "Top 5 (Increasing Seasonality)",
    row_number() > n() - 10 ~ "Bottom 5 (Decreasing Seasonality)",
    TRUE ~ "Middle"
  )) %>%
  filter(rank_group != "Middle") %>%
  group_by(rank_group) %>%
  slice_sample(n=1)

# Get detailed monthly percentage data for these parks
example_parks_cv_heatmap <- top_bottom_cv %>%
  select(park_unit, park_name, visit_raw_cv_change, rank_group) %>%
  mutate(monthly_data = map(park_unit, ~{
    visitation <- getUnitVisitation(units = .x, startYear = 2010, endYear = 2024)
    
    # Calculate monthly percentages (excluding COVID years)
    monthly_percentages <- visitation %>%
      filter(!Year %in% c(2020, 2021)) %>%
      group_by(Year) %>%
      mutate(annual_total = sum(RecreationVisitors),
             monthly_percentage = (RecreationVisitors / annual_total) * 100) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    return(monthly_percentages)
  })) %>%
  unnest(monthly_data)

# Create faceted heatmap
ggplot(example_parks_cv_heatmap, aes(x = Year, y = factor(Month, levels = 12:1, 
                                                          labels = rev(month.abb)), 
                                     fill = monthly_percentage)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "% of Annual\nVisits") +
  facet_wrap(~paste0(park_name, " (", round(visit_raw_cv_change*100, 1), "%)"), 
             ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Example Parks: Change in Monthly Visitation Distribution Over Time",
       subtitle = "Percentage of annual visits occurring in each month (COVID years excluded)",
       x = "Year", 
       y = "Month") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"))


#### Top and Bottom Parks by CV Change (Seasonality) - Time Series with Projections
# Get detailed CV trend data for these parks
example_parks_cv_trend <- top_bottom_cv %>%
  select(park_unit, park_name, visit_raw_cv_change, rank_group) %>%
  mutate(cv_trend_data = map(park_unit, ~{
    visitation <- getUnitVisitation(units = .x, startYear = 2010, endYear = 2024)
    
    # Calculate monthly percentages (excluding COVID years)
    monthly_pct <- visitation %>%
      filter(!Year %in% c(2020, 2021)) %>%
      group_by(Year) %>%
      mutate(annual_total = sum(RecreationVisitors),
             monthly_percentage = (RecreationVisitors / annual_total) * 100) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    # Calculate CV for each year
    seasonal_variation <- monthly_pct %>%
      group_by(Year) %>%
      summarize(cv_monthly = sd(monthly_percentage) / mean(monthly_percentage) * 100,
                .groups = 'drop')
    
    # Fit linear model for CV trend
    cv_model <- lm(cv_monthly ~ Year, data = seasonal_variation)
    
    # Get statistics
    r_squared <- summary(cv_model)$r.squared
    
    # Predictions for historical data
    seasonal_variation$predicted <- predict(cv_model)
    
    # Future predictions (2024-2050)
    predictions <- predict(cv_model, newdata = tibble(Year = 2024:2050), 
                           interval = "prediction", level = 0.95)
    
    future_predictions <- tibble(Year = 2024:2050,
                                 predicted_cv = predictions[,1],
                                 lower_95 = predictions[,2],
                                 upper_95 = predictions[,3])
    
    list(
      historical = seasonal_variation,
      future = future_predictions,
      r_squared = r_squared
    )
  }))

# Create individual plots for each park
cv_plots_list <- example_parks_cv_trend %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(plot = list({
    ggplot(cv_trend_data$historical, aes(x = Year)) +
      geom_line(aes(y = cv_monthly), color = "blue", size = 1) +
      geom_point(aes(y = cv_monthly), color = "blue", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_line(aes(y = predicted), color = "red", size = 1) +
      geom_point(data = cv_trend_data$future, aes(x = Year, y = predicted_cv), 
                 color = "red", size = 2, shape = 17) +
      geom_ribbon(data = cv_trend_data$future, 
                  aes(x = Year, ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95), 
                  alpha = 0.2, fill = "red") +
      annotate("rect", xmin = 2024, xmax = 2050, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
               fill = "gray90", alpha = 0.3) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 2024, linetype = "solid", 
                 color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(title = paste0(park_name, " (", park_unit, ")"),
           subtitle = paste("R² =", round(cv_trend_data$r_squared, 3), 
                            " | Projected CV Change 2024-2050 =", 
                            round(visit_raw_cv_change * 100, 1), "%"),
           x = "Year", 
           y = "Coefficient of Variation (%)") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2050, 10))
  }))

ggarrange(
  cv_plots_list$plot[[2]], 
  cv_plots_list$plot[[1]],  
  ncol = 1
)
```

#### Change in total visitation examples

Example of low (top) and high (bottom) change in visitation:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# top 5 and bottom 5 parks by percent change in visitation
top_bottom_growth <- park_visitation %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  arrange(desc(visit_raw_pct_change)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(obs_2024)) %>%
  mutate(rank_group = case_when(
    row_number() <= 10 ~ "Top 5 (Highest Growth)",
    row_number() > n() - 10 ~ "Bottom 5 (Lowest Growth)",
    TRUE ~ "Middle"
  )) %>%
  filter(rank_group != "Middle") %>%
  group_by(rank_group) %>%
  slice_sample(n=1)


top_bottom_growth <- park_visitation %>%
  filter(park_unit %in% c("PORE", "BICY")) %>%
          group_by(park_unit) %>%
  slice(1)
         
# Get detailed trend data for these parks
example_parks_growth <- top_bottom_growth %>%
  select(park_unit, park_name, visit_raw_pct_change) %>%
  mutate(trend_data = map(park_unit, ~{
    visitation <- getUnitVisitation(units = .x, startYear = 2010, endYear = 2024)
    annual_visitation <- visitation %>%
      group_by(Year) %>%
      summarize(total_visitation = sum(RecreationVisitors), .groups = "drop")
    linear_model <- lm(total_visitation ~ Year, data = annual_visitation)
    r_squared <- summary(linear_model)$r.squared
    annual_visitation$predicted <- predict(linear_model)
    predictions <- predict(linear_model, newdata = tibble(Year = 2024:2050), 
                           interval = "prediction", level = 0.95)
    
    future_predictions <- tibble(Year = 2024:2050,
                                 predicted_visitation = predictions[,1],
                                 lower_95 = predictions[,2],
                                 upper_95 = predictions[,3])
    
    list(annual = annual_visitation,
         future = future_predictions,
         r_squared = r_squared)
  }))

# plots for each park
plots_list <- example_parks_growth %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(plot = list({
    ggplot(trend_data$annual, aes(x = Year)) +
      geom_point(aes(y = total_visitation/1000000), color = "blue", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_line(aes(y = predicted/1000000), color = "red", size = 1) +
      geom_point(data = trend_data$future, aes(x = Year, y = predicted_visitation/1000000), 
                 color = "red", size = 2, shape = 17) +
      geom_ribbon(data = trend_data$future, 
                  aes(x = Year, ymin = lower_95/1000000, ymax = upper_95/1000000), 
                  alpha = 0.2, fill = "red") +
      annotate("rect", xmin = 2024, xmax = 2050, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
               fill = "gray90", alpha = 0.3) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 2024, linetype = "solid", 
                 color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(title = paste0(park_name, " (", park_unit, ")"),
           subtitle = paste("R² =", round(trend_data$r_squared, 3), 
                            " | Projected Change 2024-2050 =", 
                            round(visit_raw_pct_change, 1), "%"),
           x = "Year", 
           y = "Annual Visits (Millions)") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format()) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2050, 10))
  }))

ggarrange(
  plots_list$plot[[2]],  
  plots_list$plot[[1]],
  ncol = 1)
```
